(2) Model-quality: EXAONE does not perfectly obey all 8 prompt rules — some kept queries still contain banned subjective terms (깔끔한, 돋보인다, 심플함), fit terms (여유로운 핏, 릴렉스 핏), comfort/tactile claims (활동하기 편함, 편안한), and invented styling (다양한 하의와 매치하기 좋은). verifies.aspect: Leakage and quality of the synthetic evaluation set (synth_eval.jsonl)
verifies.findings:
PASS overall. Verified all four criteria against src/novel/gen_synth_eval.py, data/novel_cache/synth_eval.jsonl (1706 queries), src/novel/lib.py, and src/novel/run_final_suite.py.

(1) GALLERY MEMBERSHIP + TRAIN LEAK — MOSTLY OK, one minor caveat. All 1706 queries cover all 588 unique TEST gallery PIDs; 0 PIDs outside the gallery (lib.load_synth_eval also hard-raises if any appeared). HOWEVER 2 of the 588 products (2071212, 4145646) also appear in data/split_train.json AND have 3 real training pairs each in data/train_pairs_final.jsonl, so the LoRA was trained on those 2 products. The synth-eval query text is independently generated (not verbatim the training queries), but the products themselves were seen in training. This is a pre-existing train/test SPLIT overlap (the raw splits share these 2 PIDs), not introduced by the generator. Impact = 6/1706 queries = 0.35%. Negligible, below the fatal-critique floor, but worth a one-line caveat in the report.

(2) CASUAL USER STYLE, NOT CAPTION COPY — PASS. Judged 20 random samples vs their formal text_description: queries are short, casual, observation-based (color + category + graphic), clearly distinct from the formal marketing captions. 0 verbatim caption echoes across the full set. The generation prompt (prompts/augment_final.txt) aggressively bans brand metadata, fit jargon, and subjective adjectives. Minor quality nits (not failures): the prompt's own rules occasionally leak through — one q3 contains meta-commentary '(여기서는 그래픽과 색상을 강조하였습니다.)', and a handful retain banned fit terms (오버핏/릴렉스 핏/머슬핏) or negation phrasing (고양이 그림이 없는). Mild, not distribution-breaking.

(3) NO DEGENERATE/EMPTY/DUP DOMINATION — PASS. 0 empty queries. Only 1 exact-duplicate row, and it is two DIFFERENT products sharing a generic short query ('화이트 컬러의 긴팔 크루 넥 티셔츠'), not a within-product collapse. 1705/1706 unique. Length 13–120 chars (mean 53.7, median 49). Coverage: 531 products with 3 queries, 56 with 2, only 1 with a single query. qtype balanced (q1_short 588 / q2_medium 556 / q3_aspect 562).

(4) HUBNESS BANK = TRAIN SYNTHETIC BANK, NOT SYNTH EVAL — PASS. In run_final_suite.py, apply() uses B = c.bank(enc) = cached bank_q (7023 TRAIN synthetic queries from train_pairs_final.jsonl). Every hubness method (modality_gap, qbnorm_dis, qbnorm_mul, csls, aqe) draws its population statistics from B, never from synth['enc']/synth['texts']. The 1706 synth-eval queries are only the scored queries Q. 0 synth-eval queries overlap the train bank verbatim.

Files: /root/code/jolnon/src/novel/gen_synth_eval.py, /root/code/jolnon/data/novel_cache/synth_eval.jsonl, /root/code/jolnon/src/novel/lib.py, /root/code/jolnon/src/novel/run_final_suite.py, /root/code/jolnon/data/split_train.json, /root/code/jolnon/data/train_pairs_final.jsonl.

VERDICT: Statistics machinery is correct and HP selection is clean. But the ONE "method beats current-best" significance claim on human-30 is fragile (rests on 9 non-tie queries) and disappears against the honest published reference. Defensibility floor is met; the strong claim is not.

(1) HP SELECTION ISOLATION — PASS. Static + dynamic checks confirm every hyperparameter is chosen on VALIDATION only:
- Correction HP via best_hp_on_val() scores solely on c.vq(enc)/Gv/vgt (240-product val gallery, train-split synthetic queries). /root/code/jolnon/src/novel/run_final_suite.py:156-165.
- All three BM25 (n,w) grid searches (lines 116-120, 185-189, 203-207) select on lib.rerank_topn(..., val_bm25, ...) against vgt, then apply the FROZEN (n,w) to eval (eval_bm25) and synth (synth_bm25). Never selected on human-30 (egt) or synth (synth gt). Correction+BM25 mode fixes the method HP to the standalone val-best first, then grids BM25 on val — no joint peeking at test.

(2) PAIRED SIGN TEST / BOOTSTRAP — PASS, reproduced independently from the published rank arrays. lib.paired_compare (lib.py:266-305) and lib.bootstrap_ci (249-263) operate on per-query reciprocal ranks (1/rank). Sign test uses scipy.stats.binomtest(wins, wins+losses, 0.5) — correct exact two-sided test with ties properly excluded from n. Independent recompute: max |reported eval_MRR - recomputed| = 4.8e-5; bootstrap CI for lora384 identity reproduced exactly [0.537,0.825]; sign tests reproduced exactly (e.g. qbnorm_mul+bm25 vs repro: 8W/1L, p=0.039).

(3) SYNTH EVAL GT INDEXES THE SAME 588 GALLERY — PASS. load_synth_eval maps product_id through meta.json gallery_pids (588, identical to load_data ordering — verified equal). synth gt min/max = 0/587 (< 588); recomputed gt matches; all 1706 synth queries cover the same 588 gallery products. human eval_gt max 574 < 588; val_gt max 239 < 240.

(4) CURRENT-BEST COMPARISON HONESTY — PASS. lora384_bm25_pub (0.756) is loaded from the published detail json (output/eval_hybrid_rerank_top10_015bm25_detail.json, 30 queries, recomputed MRR = 0.7560 exactly). The in-harness lora384_bm25_repro (0.7212) is separately labeled and the comment at top of the file explicitly states the repro under-performs the published number because of the proper small-weight grid; the two are kept distinct in refs_eval. Honest.

ARTIFACT / OVERCLAIM RISKS (the substantive findings):
- The best human-30 method, qbnorm_mul+bm25 lora384 (eval_MRR 0.7636), is "significant" vs the in-harness repro (0.7212) at sign_p=0.039 — but this rests on only 9 non-tie queries out of 30 (8 wins, 1 loss, 21 ties). Against the HONEST published current-best (0.756), the same method's delta is only +0.0076 with sign_p=0.688 — NOT significant. So the headline "beats current-best" holds only against the weaker repro, not the published baseline. Any claim of beating the published 0.756 is an artifact of small-n and of comparing to the lower repro number.
- Multiplicity: 24 method-vs-bm25_repro comparisons on human-30; Bonferroni threshold would be 0.05/24 = 0.0021. NONE of the p<0.05 rows survive. The suite reports raw p-values with no correction (acceptable for a capstone, but a "significant" label on any single row is not robust).
- 6 of the 7 p<0.05 eval rows are in the WRONG direction (negative mean_delta — the base-encoder methods LOSE to the BM25 baseline; the sign test is merely confirming the baseline wins). Only the qbnorm_mul+bm25 lora384 row is a genuine method-win, and it is the fragile one above.
- Synth-eval significances (p≈0.0 with N=1706) are statistically real but the synth set is dominated by BM25-favorable lexical overlap (dense_bm25 synth_MRR jumps to 0.90 vs 0.72 on human-30), so synth significance reflects the BM25 lever, not the correction methods (correction +bm25 vs bm25_repro on synth is near-zero delta, e.g. qbnorm_mul +bm25: -0.0001, p=1.0).

MINOR PRE-EXISTING LEAK (not a suite bug, below defensibility floor): 2 of the 588 gallery product_ids (2071212, 4145646) also appear in train_pairs_final.jsonl (3 train pairs each), i.e. the LoRA saw queries for 2 test products. Impact: 6/1706 synth queries (0.35%) and 0/30 human queries target these. Negligible; originates in the upstream split, not in run_final_suite.py.

Bottom line: the statistics code is correct and the protocol (val-only HP, paired tests on per-query RR, same 588 gallery, honest published ref) is sound. The defensible claim — "our test-time method is competitive with / slightly above the published BM25 current-best on human-30 and clearly helps the base encoder on the high-power synth eval" — holds. A strong claim of a SIGNIFICANT win over the published 0.756 baseline on human-30 would be an artifact (p=0.688 vs pub; only 9 informative queries; no multiplicity correction).

final.headline: On the gold human-30 eval (the contracted evaluation, but very low power, MRR 95% CIs roughly +/-0.13), the LoRA text-adapter beats zero-shot SigLIP (0.684 vs 0.571) and the dense+BM25 hybrid is the strongest standalone-scoring baseline; no test-time correction we added beats the published current-best of 0.756 with statistical support. On the high-power synthetic eval (N=1706 user-style queries over the same 588 unseen test products), the same picture holds with much tighter CIs, and it reveals two genuinely-supported findings: (1) every test-time correction that reuses the train synthetic-query bank as a statistical prior (modality_gap, qbnorm_dis/mul, CSLS) gives a small but significant lift over the LoRA cosine baseline standalone, and (2) when stacked on dense+BM25, modality_gap (+0.0057, p=0) and AQE (+0.0046, p=0.0012) significantly edge the strong dense+BM25 baseline on synth — but these gains are sub-1 MRR-point and are NOT reproduced as significant on human-30, so they are best described as a consistent positive trend confirmed at higher power, not a win on the gold eval. The verified, robust story is: LoRA > zero-shot, and BM25 fusion > dense-only; the bank-as-prior corrections are a real-but-marginal extra.
final.table_markdown:
| Method | enc | Standalone eval MRR | Standalone synth MRR | +BM25 eval MRR | +BM25 synth MRR | Sig vs LoRA cosine (synth) | Sig vs dense+BM25 repro (synth) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Zero-shot (identity) | base | 0.5711 | 0.4312 | 0.5476 | 0.8204 | n/a (below LoRA) | no |
| LoRA cosine (identity) | lora384 | 0.6842 | 0.5684 | 0.7212 (dense+BM25) | 0.9026 (dense+BM25) | reference | reference (the +BM25 row) |
| modality_gap | lora384 | 0.7059 | 0.5698 | 0.7337 | 0.9083 | YES (+0.0014, p=0.011) | YES (+0.0057, p=0.0) |
| qbnorm_dis | lora384 | 0.7190 | 0.5712 | 0.7053 | 0.9090 | YES (+0.0028, p=0.0049) | NO (+0.0065, p=0.090) |
| qbnorm_mul | lora384 | 0.7074 | 0.5724 | 0.7636 | 0.9024 | YES (+0.0039, p=0.014) | NO (-0.0001, p=1.0) |
| csls | lora384 | 0.6809 | 0.5848 | 0.7602 | 0.9059 | YES (+0.0164, p=0.0004) | NO (+0.0033, p=0.60) |
| aqe | lora384 | 0.7133 | 0.5605 | 0.7200 | 0.9072 | NO (-0.0079, negative) | YES (+0.0046, p=0.0012) |
| Published current-best | lora384 | — | — | 0.756 | (not on synth) | — | — |

Notes: standalone "eval MRR" gains for the corrections (e.g. qbnorm_dis 0.719, aqe 0.7133) look large on human-30 but are within the +/-0.13 CI and none is significant vs LoRA on human-30 (best sign-test p approx 0.18). The +BM25 eval column: only qbnorm_mul (0.7636) is significant vs the in-harness repro 0.7212 on human-30 (delta +0.0425, p=0.039, 8W/1L) — but NOT significant vs the published 0.756 (delta +0.0076, p=0.688). dense+BM25 lora384 is the current-best baseline (eval 0.7212 repro / 0.756 published; synth 0.9026).
verified_wins_vs_baseline: LoRA text adapter beats zero-shot SigLIP on BOTH evals: human-30 0.6842 vs 0.5711; synth 0.5684 vs 0.4312 with a tight CI [0.55,0.587] vs [0.412,0.451] (synth sign-test 905W/257L over zero-shot, p=0.0). This is the core thesis claim and it is robustly supported.

BM25 lexical fusion beats dense-only retrieval on the high-power synth eval by a large, unambiguous margin for the LoRA encoder: dense+BM25 0.9026 vs LoRA-cosine 0.5684 (synth delta +0.3341, p=0.0, 893W/66L). On human-30 the same fusion is 0.7212 (repro) / 0.756 (published) vs 0.6842 LoRA-cosine (directionally up, within CI).

Every bank-as-prior correction that reuses the train synthetic-query bank as a test-time statistical prior gives a small but statistically significant standalone lift over the LoRA cosine baseline on the high-power synth eval: csls +0.0164 (p=0.0004), qbnorm_mul +0.0039 (p=0.0137), qbnorm_dis +0.0028 (p=0.0049), modality_gap +0.0014 (p=0.011). (AQE standalone is the lone exception: -0.0079, negative, excluded.) These are sub-2 MRR-point gains, significant only because N=1706.
verified_wins_vs_current_best: NONE that survive an honest, conservative reading. The dense+BM25 hybrid (synth 0.9026; human-30 0.756 published / 0.7212 repro) is the current best, and no method beats it with support on BOTH eval sets.

On synth only (high power), two corrections stacked on dense+BM25 are statistically significant over the dense+BM25 repro baseline: modality_gap+BM25 (0.9083, delta +0.0057, p=0.0) and AQE+BM25 (0.9072, delta +0.0046, p=0.0012). These are real at N=1706 but are sub-0.6 MRR-point gains and are NOT significant on human-30 (modality_gap eval delta +0.0125, p=0.125; AQE eval delta -0.0012, n.s.). Per the brief these qualify as 'consistent positive trend confirmed at higher power', NOT 'beats current-best on the gold eval'.

The human-30 top scorer, qbnorm_mul+BM25 (eval 0.7636), is significant vs the in-harness repro (0.7212, p=0.039) but NOT vs the published 0.756 (delta +0.0076, p=0.688), and on synth it is dead-even with dense+BM25 (-0.0001, p=1.0). So its apparent human-30 'win' rests on 9 non-tie queries and comparison to the weaker repro number; it is an artifact of small-n, not a defensible win over the published baseline.
No single method dominates both eval sets: the synth-significant winners (modality_gap, AQE) are not the human-30 winner (qbnorm_mul), and none clears the published 0.756 with significance.
final.real_vs_noise: "What N=30 cannot resolve and N=1706 can: On human-30 the MRR CIs are roughly +/-0.13, so almost everything from LoRA (0.684) up through dense+BM25 (0.756) is statistically indistinguishable; the apparent standalone-correction 'lifts' (e.g. qbnorm_dis 0.719, aqe 0.7133 vs LoRA 0.684) and the apparent qbnorm_mul+BM25 'win' (0.7636) all live inside or near that band and rest on a handful of non-tie queries (qbnorm_mul+BM25 sig is 8W/1L out of 30, 21 ties). Human-30 simply cannot tell these apart. The synth eval, with ~57x more queries and CIs of +/-0.02, resolves the ordering cleanly and reveals three things invisible at N=30: (1) the LoRA>zero-shot and BM25>dense effects are huge and unambiguous (deltas 0.13-0.33, p=0); (2) the bank-as-prior corrections produce a small but genuine, repeatable positive signal standalone (csls/qbnorm/modality_gap all p<0.05) that human-30 reported as noise; (3) once dense+BM25 is in place, the corrections' added value collapses to sub-1 MRR-point, and only modality_gap and AQE clear significance — i.e. BM25 already captures most of what the corrections were fixing. Where the two evals AGREE: LoRA beats zero-shot, BM25 fusion beats dense-only, and no correction is a large win over dense+BM25. Where they DISAGREE: human-30 crowns qbnorm_mul+BM25 (which synth says is even with dense+BM25), while synth crowns modality_gap/AQE+BM25 (which human-30 says is noise). This disagreement is itself the honest finding: the marginal-correction gains are at the resolution limit, direction-consistent at best, and should not be reported as a head-to-head win on the gold eval. One caveat carried from verification: the synth eval shares 2 of 588 products with the train split (6/1706 queries = 0.35%, pre-existing in the repo splits, identical exposure for all methods) — negligible and below the fatal-critique floor, but worth a one-line footnote."
final.thesis_narrative: "Frame the contribution as: the distribution gap between catalogue captions and real user queries is the dominant weakness of zero-shot retrieval, and a parameter-efficient text-only LoRA trained on LLM-generated user-style queries closes most of it (0.571 -> 0.684 on the gold human-30 eval; 0.431 -> 0.568 on a high-power synthetic user-query eval, both p=0). That is the headline, defensible result and it is confirmed at high power. The secondary, more novel angle is to REPURPOSE the synthetic query bank built for training as a TEST-TIME statistical prior: the same 7k synthetic queries that aligned the encoder can, at inference, supply the population statistics for distribution-correction operators (QB-Norm, CSLS, modality-gap centering; AQE for expansion). This is a new USE of an existing asset, orthogonal to BM25, dual-tower, or a learned reranker, and costs nothing extra to obtain. Honestly scoped, the bank-as-prior corrections yield a small-but-significant standalone improvement over the tuned encoder (high power confirms what N=30 could not), but their marginal value largely overlaps with lexical BM25 fusion: once dense+BM25 is applied, only modality-gap centering and AQE retain a significant (sub-1 MRR-point) edge on the high-power eval, and none beats the published dense+BM25 number on the gold eval with statistical support. The defensible thesis is therefore: (a) text-side alignment to the user-query distribution is the highest-leverage intervention (large, robust); (b) reusing the synthetic bank as a test-time prior is a cheap, conceptually clean add-on that gives a consistent, high-power-confirmed positive trend; (c) BM25 fusion is the single best practical lever and the corrections are complementary-but-marginal on top of it. Do not claim a state-of-the-art win over the current best; claim a coherent, well-powered demonstration that distribution alignment (train-time via LoRA, optionally test-time via the reused bank) beats the zero-shot baseline and is competitive with the strong hybrid."
final.recommendation: "Report dense+BM25 on the LoRA encoder as the headline operating point (human-30 0.756 published / 0.7212 repro; synth 0.9026), and present the bank-as-prior corrections as a complementary contribution, not a winner over current-best. Concretely: (1) Lead with the two robust, dual-confirmed claims — LoRA beats zero-shot, and BM25 fusion beats dense-only — these carry the capstone. (2) Present the bank-as-prior corrections with honest framing: standalone they give a small significant lift over LoRA cosine on the high-power eval (csls/qbnorm/modality_gap, all p<0.05), demonstrating the synthetic bank has test-time value; stacked on BM25 the gain shrinks to sub-1 MRR-point and only modality_gap (+0.0057) and AQE (+0.0046) stay significant on synth. Describe these as 'a consistent positive trend, confirmed at higher power' and explicitly state they are NOT a significant win on the human-30 gold eval. (3) If forced to name ONE best system, pick modality_gap+BM25: it has the top synth MRR among corrections (0.9083), is significant vs dense+BM25 on synth, and is directionally positive on human-30 (0.7337) — it is the most defensible single recommendation. Avoid headlining qbnorm_mul+BM25's 0.7636: its human-30 'significance' is vs the weaker repro only, evaporates against the published 0.756, and is flat on synth. (4) Always quote the synth gain in absolute MRR points (it is <1 point) alongside the p-value, so no reader mistakes statistical significance for practical magnitude. (5) Footnote the 2-product (6-query, 0.35%) train/test overlap as a pre-existing, method-neutral split artifact. Given the one-week budget and 'beat-baseline' bar, the existing results are sufficient to write up now — no further experiments needed; the work is in honest framing, not more runs."
